question.text: USDINR spot is 83. Indian risk-free rate is 7% and US risk-free rate is 5%. What is the fair 6-month USDINR futures price using interest rate parity?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using interest rate parity: F = S × (1 + R_INR × t) / (1 + R_USD × t) = 83 × (1 + 0.07 × 0.5) / (1 + 0.05 × 0.5) = 83 × 1.035 / 1.025 = 83 × 1.009756… ≈ Rs. 83.8097, which rounds to Rs. 83.81. The Currency Derivatives workbook gives the same exact value for this calculation. The Trap: Rs. 84.66 uses the full annual rate differential instead of the 6-month fraction. Rs. 82.21 wrongly inverts the formula (dividing by the INR rate instead of the USD rate). Rs. 83.79 is a slightly under-rounded variant that does not match the source's exact figure. Note: In IRP, the currency with the higher interest rate (here INR) trades at a forward premium that reflects the rate differential — the workbook also gives an approximate shortcut of about Rs. 83.83 for the same inputs.
